verification_report.summary: The proof is correct under the explicitly accepted inputs and the book's standing compact connected setting. The Q-representative map defines a finite metric on all-positive-weight multiplier-ideal classes; the metric is totally bounded and separable, its canonical completion is the L1 closure of the fixed-point set, and smooth positive volume changes give bi-Lipschitz equivalent metrics. On a compact connected curve with positive unit-mass theta, finite atomic Green potentials are normalized Q- and P-fixed points with zero non-pluripolar measure. Their density in all K_theta, incompleteness of the ideal-class metric, and L1 discontinuity of Q follow from the checked mass-exhaustion, distributional uniqueness and compactness arguments. The formal theorem concerns real logarithmic poles; choosing rational atomic probabilities also gives the analytic-density version in the source's rational-coefficient convention. No global BMP or identification with d_S is used. All checks and the coefficient clarification are recorded in results/ideal_lone_completion_01/fullreport.md.
